answer: Reciprocal edge audit. Each identity must maintain at least two long-lived, reciprocally confirmed links whose endpoints independently report the same connection. Sybil clusters create dense internal edges but few inbound confirmations from established regions; the audit scores a velvet boundary of cross-region reciprocity. An attacker must sustain real two-way traffic through a canyon of unrelated hosts, paying bandwidth and maintenance per fake identity. Isolated clusters fail like a glacier calving: edges drop and identities lose standing.
